label: cex-composition-of-relations-is-not-commutative
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY:
- u = ∅ (empty set): well-defined by L6, has no elements, so u ≠ v.
- v = {∅} (singleton of empty): well-defined by L5, has one element (∅), so u ≠ v is proved.
- A = {u,v}: a two-element set; R and S are subsets of A×A, so they are relations on A as claimed.
- R and S are nonempty singletons; the counterexample does not rely on empty relations.
- S∘R and R∘S are nonempty; the proof does not need to treat the empty composite as a boundary case.
- Ordered pairs with identical coordinates (u,u) and (v,v): L3 gives the equality condition; u ≠ v ensures they are distinct, so S∘R ≠ R∘S.
- Associativity (L8) is only mentioned, not used in the construction, so no circularity.
- All objects are well-founded sets; no hidden assumptions about proper classes or undefined terms.

CHECKED: Read every numbered step (1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1) and every cited fact (L1–L9) against the supplied dependency texts; each fact is a faithful rendering and each step is mathematically licensed by the cited material.
